content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Coats-Observatory's PostCoats-ObservatoryMarch 13, 2025 · Shared with PublicThe media has been making quite a song and dance about the forthcoming lunar eclipse, with the usual headlines of a 'Blood Moon' being visible. Whilst the Moon can turn a deep red during a lunar eclipse this is not something we are going to be able to see from our location this time round.A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth passes between the Moon and the Sun, with the Earth casting its shadow onto the lunar surface and darkening it into the process. The red colour occurs at maximum eclipse due to a phenomenon known as "Rayleigh Scattering", where the blue end of the spectrum gets scattered by the Earth's atmosphere, leaving only the red end and so turning the Moon that colour.Paisley is not in the best position to view the eclipse unfortunately. From our location the Moon will start to dim just after 5am on Friday, 14 March. The Moon sets just over an hour later, so all we will see is a small portion of the Moon darkening before it has gone below the horizon. If you are fortunate enough to be in North or South America you will be treated to the full show, clear skies dependent of course.The next total lunar eclipse visible from Paisley falls on 07 September, 2025, although we won't see the 'Blood Moon' then as that part of the eclipse will be over by the time the Moon rises. After that there are total lunar eclipses on 31 December 2028, 26 June 2029 and 20 December 2029.For more information on lunar eclipses and the when, where, why and how of them please visit https://science.nasa.gov/eclipses/There will be a partial solar eclipse visible from Paisley on March 29 - more on that later though!(The image is a simulated view using our planetarium software showing the extent of the eclipse as visible from Paisley.)All reactions:561 comment11 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Stephen BarclayI am disappointed we will not see the eclipse on the 7th , I was hoping to go up the breas to see it , I have read we could well see the moon coming out of it around 7.30pm32w All reactions:561 comment11 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Stephen BarclayI am disappointed we will not see the eclipse on the 7th , I was hoping to go up the breas to see it , I have read we could well see the moon coming out of it around 7.30pm32w
